title: Read labels and SDS
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply: read labels and sds

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Learning goal and job context: This lesson teaches read labels and sds for routine cleaning work. Start with the actual job scope, site instructions, manufacturer directions and worker training. Never treat a general lesson as authority to perform restricted or specialist work.

Core procedure: Locate product identity, hazard pictograms, directions, first-aid, storage and disposal on the container. Match the exact product and formulation to its current SDS; use SDS sections on hazards, handling, exposure controls, first aid and spills rather than relying on a generic product family.

Decision-making in the field: Before acting, ask: What is the surface or equipment? What is the soil or hazard? Which product or method is approved? What could harm a person, property or food? If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

Worked workplace scenario: A replacement bottle has a similar brand name but a different dilution instruction. The worker stops and checks the exact label and SDS before preparing the solution.

Guided supervised practice: Provide two mock labels and SDS excerpts; identify five differences and complete a product-authorisation checklist.

Evidence and feedback: The assessor observes the task and checks whether the learner: identifies correct product, site-approved use, ppe and emergency information without guessing. A learner must explain any unsafe choice, correct it and repeat the demonstration. Record observations, required coaching and reassessment rather than awarding competence from attendance alone.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Read the product identity, hazard pictograms, directions, first-aid, storage and disposal details on the container.
Match the exact product and formulation to its current safety data sheet (SDS), and do not rely on a similar brand name or a product family.
Read the SDS sections on hazards, handling, exposure controls, first aid and spills.
Check the dilution and use directions on the label against the approved method for the surface or equipment before mixing or applying.
Ask what the surface or equipment is, what the soil or hazard is, and what could harm a person, property or food.
If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.
Check the label and SDS again whenever a replacement bottle or a different product is used.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: The exact product and formulation are matched to its current SDS before use.
Label directions for dilution, PPE and first aid are identified without guessing.
The surface, soil, approved method and possible harm are considered before acting, and an unclear answer means pausing for supervisor guidance.
Any unsafe choice is explained and corrected, and competence is recorded from observation rather than attendance.
summary: The product label is read first for product identity, hazard pictograms, directions, first aid, storage and disposal.
The exact product and formulation are matched to the current SDS, using its hazard, handling, exposure control, first aid and spill sections rather than a generic product family.
A replacement bottle with a different dilution instruction is checked against its exact label and SDS before any solution is prepared.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you check before performing read labels and sds?
options: The brand name, because similar brands have the same instructions
The product's colour and smell, which show its strength
The exact product and formulation, matched to its current label and SDS
The label on the old bottle you used last time

knowledgeChecks.question: What do you do if the method, product or equipment is unsafe or uncertain?
options: Use the product you know best and check the label later
Ask the client to choose the product
Pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance
Guess the dilution from the bottle's colour
